content: Oral torus refers to a bony growth composed of dense, compact bone that develops within the oral cavity, either along the palate or the mandible. When this growth occurs along the midline of the palate, it is referred to as a palatal torus or torus palatinus. Conversely, when it develops on the lingual (tongue-facing) side of the mandible, it is called a mandibular torus or torus mandibularis. The prevalence of oral tori is higher in women compared to men. These bony growths are typically associated with adulthood and are rarely observed in individuals under the age of 15. Palatal tori are particularly more common among Native American and Inuit populations. Treatment for oral tori is generally unnecessary unless they interfere with normal chewing function or the fitting of prosthetic dental appliances.
